Subject: Post-call: HIPAA/BAA eligibility & next steps

Hi Samantha / Robert —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve attached a short security overview and a redacted SOC 2 Type II report for your security team to review.

Recap (high level)
- SOC 2 / Privacy: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II (redacted report attached) and maintains GDPR-aligned controls for EU customers.
- HIPAA / BAA: We offer a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for eligible customers. A BAA is required before we can accept or persist PHI.
- PHI handling / eligible deployment modes:
  - Hosted (public Redwood API): NOT eligible for PHI or customer-identifiable health data. Hosted may be used for non-PHI workloads only.
  - Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): Eligible for PHI once a BAA is signed and appropriate configuration (networking + KMS) is in place.
  - Private (VPC / on-prem): Eligible for PHI; recommended for regulated environments that require customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM.
- Key management & audit: For Dedicated/Private we support customer KMS integrations and provide audit logs and retention controls you can configure.

Open / next steps we agreed on
1) MedHealth to confirm whether the PoC will include PHI or de-identified data (Samantha) — owner: MedHealth — ETA: 6/20
2) Redwood to send vendor security questionnaire + SOC2 (done) and BAA template via DocuSign (links below) — owner: Marissa / Dylan — ETA: 6/19
3) If MedHealth needs PHI processing, we'll schedule a technical call to review Dedicated vs Private configuration and KMS options — owner: Marissa / Solutions Eng — ETA: week of 6/24

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Overview.pdf, SOC2_Type2_redacted.pdf, BAA_template.docx
DocuSign BAA: https://docusign.com/rdw/BAA/RDW-BAA-2029-0134
Security docs: https://app.redwood.ai/docs/security#hipaa

If I missed anything from the call or you want different owners / dates, say so and I’ll update the MAP.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

Thanks Samantha — good questions. Quick answers below and a couple of follow-ups.

1) Hosted API and metadata: Hosted public endpoints are not cleared for PHI. That includes patient identifiers and any PII/PHI in request payloads or headers. If you need to pass identifiers for routing, we recommend either de-identifying before sending or using Dedicated/Private where you control the network boundaries and KMS.

2) Logs & retention for Dedicated: By default, Dedicated is provisioned to send audit logs to the customer-managed logging endpoint when PHI is enabled. We can configure retention to zero on Redwood side and forward logs to your S3/ELK. We'll document the exact flow in the technical call.

BAA & contract notes:
- We can execute our standard BAA with MedHealth (DocuSign link below). If you require amendments (e.g., indemnity language), please flag the specific clauses and we'll route to Legal for review. Typical turnaround for simple signature is ~5 business days; redlines may take 2–4 weeks depending on scope.

Technical items that will help the PoC:
- Confirm whether test data for initial integration will be PHI or de-identified.
- If PHI, we will provision a Dedicated environment and open a security onboarding ticket to configure KMS and log forwarding.

I’ll have Dylan kick off the vendor security questionnaire via SecureFile and he’ll be your point for the SOC2/artifact exchange.

DocuSign BAA: https://docusign.com/rdw/BAA/RDW-BAA-2029-0134

Action: Samantha — confirm PHI vs de-id by 6/20; Robert — loop Legal if you anticipate redlines to BAA.
